business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border E-Commerce Overseas Warehouse Order Fulfillment

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa (Unitary National Jurisdiction, no sub-state tax distinctions)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Common Law statutory framework with customary law overlay recognized under the Constitution; corporate and financial legislation modeled on Pacific-Commonwealth precedents and OECD-compliant offshore drafting
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER Plus - Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (signed 2017, in force 2020)
Agreement between Samoa and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion (signed 2013)
Cotonou Partnership Agreement (EU-ACP) and successor SAMOA Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2018 (Samoa AML/CFT Act 2018), administered by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit and the Central Bank of Samoa; International Companies Act 2018 (ICA 2018), Part on Registered Agents, Directors, Shareholders and Significant Owners; International Companies (Fees) Regulations 2018; Central Bank of Samoa AML/CFT Rules and FIU Directives; Companies Act 2001 (for domestic comparators)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport of each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of residence (People's Republic of China)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the China Ministry of Foreign Affairs; Samoa is a receiving State under the Hague Apostille Convention and accepts the foreign apostille without consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors and UBO Declaration Form (UB-1)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (Apostille Office) if the document is to be used abroad; otherwise accepted as a private instrument for domestic filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified translation of the all-Chinese Articles of Association (章程) and Chinese business license of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public and licensed translation service in the People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the notarized translation and source license; alternative consular legalization through the Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs occurs only when the source jurisdiction is not an Apostille Contracting State

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and professional introduction letter from the institutional payment provider or upstream bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or licensed payment institution (e.g., Airwallex partner bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private authentication by the beneficiary institution; no apostille or consular legalization required where the recipient accepts the bank's registered electronic verification and letterhead

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding and continuous screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs and signatories against Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) databases, the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, the Samoan domestic sanctions list, and INTERPOL notices; enhanced due diligence is required for PEP relationships including 12-month periodic reviews, source-of-wealth verification, and senior management sign-off; all screening records and beneficial ownership records must be retained for a minimum of five years under the AML/CFT Act 2018

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registrar of International Companies (RIC), Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) - Samoa Companies and International Companies Registry online name-search and reservation facility, Apia
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory registered name must be in Latin script (English or Samoan); a Chinese or other non-Latin script may be used as a secondary trading name only where a notarized romanized transliteration is filed; all-Chinese Articles of Association are accepted as internal governance documents provided a certified English or Samoan translation is filed with the RIC; the name must end with a recognized corporate designator such as 'Limited' or 'Ltd' unless exempted
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name application is submitted through the RIC/MCIL online facility with the requisite fee; the Registrar issues a rejection notice citing the specific statutory ground; the applicant may file a written administrative review request with the Registrar within 14 business days of the rejection, providing evidence of the proposed name's distinctiveness and lawful use; if the review is refused, an appeal may be submitted to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 30 days of the refusal; a granted reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 days upon payment of the prescribed extension fee before the reservation lapses

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible only through the licensed Samoan registered agent's physical office address in Apia, which serves as the statutory registered office; a standalone virtual mailbox without a licensed Samoan registered agent is not permissible for an International Company under the ICA 2018; an ISIC 5210 cross-dock/overseas 3PL operation may hold contracts and payment rails offshore while the operational fulfillment center is located in the destination market; no in-country physical warehouse is required for the Samoan entity
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - estimated annual unannounced inspection probability below 5% for a clean, low-risk international company; the risk may increase if the registered agent is selected for an FIU thematic inspection, a Central Bank AML/CFT examination, or during an Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) mutual evaluation cycle

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), ss. 6 (Incorporation), 7 (Memorandum and Articles), 8 (Registered Office), 28 (Directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Form IC-1 Application for Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; at least one share must be issued but need not be paid up. No escrow account required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the subscriptions of the founding shareholder for 1 ordinary share at USD 1.00 each are accepted and the share register is duly opened; (2) the registered office of the Company at [address in Apia, Samoa], as designated by the registered agent, is adopted as the official address for service of process and all statutory records; (3) [Director Name] is appointed as the first director of the Company, and shall hold office until the first annual general meeting or earlier removal; (4) the registered agent is authorized to file all incorporation documents and to affix the common seal; and (5) any one director is authorized to open bank accounts and execute banking mandates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IC-0 (Name Reservation) with up to three proposed names. Confirm availability and obtain non-objection. The chosen name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.' and must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised Form IC-0 with a modified name or provide a written explanation by the registered agent demonstrating distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent under SIFA oversight
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in accordance with the International Companies Act 1987, incorporating the standard provisions required for an International Company. The founding shareholder executes the documents, and the registered agent countersigns as nominee holder of the registered office.
required_dossiers: Identification of shareholder and intended director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries any clause as inconsistent with the Act, revise the relevant provision and re-file the amended constitutional documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form IC-1 together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, consent of the registered agent, registered office confirmation, and statutory filing fee. The application may be submitted physically at the SIFA registry in Apia or through the approved electronic filing portal.
required_dossiers: Copy of director's and shareholder's passport or national identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a Notice of Query is issued, respond in writing within 14 days with clarifications, additional evidence, or proposed amendments; otherwise the application will be deemed withdrawn and a fresh filing will be required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Company Seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the common seal. The first board resolution is then formally recorded, share certificates are issued to the founding shareholder, and the statutory registers are opened.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains typographical or legal deficiencies, file a rectification request under section 120 of the International Companies Act for correction without re-application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Corporate Governance and Annual Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to adopt the pro-forma resolution, appoint officers, approve the bank account mandate, and confirm the corporate compliance calendar. Notify the registered agent of any ongoing obligations, including annual fees and statutory filing deadlines.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an annual return or annual fee is inadvertently missed, file the late submission with the applicable late penalty through the registered agent to restore good standing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – International Company operates outside Samoa; no domestic industrial licence is required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – offshore cross-dock and 3PL operation with no physical development in Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No Samoa-based discharges; overseas warehouse facilities must comply with host-country wastewater, VOC emission, and solid waste handling regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable – no physical premises in Samoa. If a domestic facility were established, fire safety certification from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA), structural inspection approval, and workplace registration with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) would be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Government of Samoa — tax administration and online services portal (MfR e-Services / Lafeta)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity not otherwise carrying on a taxable Samoa activity is not required to hold a Samoan TIN. However, a non-resident supplier that meets the VAGST registration threshold must apply to the Ministry for Revenue using Form TIN/VAGST Registration, submit its certificate of incorporation, the foreign entity's constitutional and registry documents, and a letter of intent. The Ministry assigns a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and, if applicable, a VAGST registration number. A Samoa International Company that remains within the statutory tax-exempt regime does not file an income tax return and does not undertake VAGST registration unless it makes a taxable supply in Samoa; where exemption is desired in documentary form, an application for a Certificate of Tax Exemption may be made under the International Companies Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not operate an elective check-the-box classification for foreign purposes. A Samoa International Company is tax-exempt by statutory default under the International Companies Act, and no hybrid mismatch or entity classification election is available before Samoa's Ministry for Revenue. If the International Company elects to carry on business within Samoa or to obtain Samoan-source income outside the exempt perimeter, it thereby self-assumes ordinary company tax treatment and becomes registrable for VAGST and income tax; no other elective mechanism exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 of taxable supplies in a 12-month period, or the lower threshold prescribed for non-resident suppliers of certain services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time electronic-invoicing clearance, API filing, or fiscal digital stamping regime applies as of the current Samoa tax administration. VAGST-registered suppliers must issue a tax invoice containing the prescribed particulars under the Tax Administration Act and keep the underlying records accessible to the Ministry for Revenue. VAGST returns are filed electronically through the MfR online portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available in Samoa for goods that are exported from Samoa to a destination outside Samoa, provided the goods are removed from Samoa in accordance with the Customs Act and an approved export entry is lodged. Services supplied by a Samoan entity are zero-rated when they are supplied to a recipient outside Samoa and are physically performed outside Samoa, or when the services are directly related to exported goods under the VAGST rules. An offshore 3PL and order-fulfillment hub operated by a Samoa International Company may zero-rate its paid services to non-resident e-commerce sellers if the service recipient is non-resident, the services relate to goods located outside Samoa, or the services are provided solely to the non-resident party with no local consumption or benefit.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Samoa Customs and the Ministry for Revenue may audit zero-rated export claims retrospectively. If an export zero-rating is unsupported by the prescribed export documentation or the sales proceeds are not repatriated within the 180-day deadline, the claim is clawed back in full with VAGST assessed at 15%, plus late payment interest and a shortfall penalty under the Tax Administration Act. Fraudulent zero-rating claims carry criminal penalties including monetary fines and, for bodies corporate, fines on the entity and on each director or officer; in serious cases the court may impose a custodial sentence on responsible officers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 2002; foreign exchange administration is delegated under the Exchange Control Act 1975, the Exchange Control Regulations 1976, and the Central Bank's Exchange Control Guidelines and Authorized Dealer Notices
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) operates under a managed float. Samoa has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations, so current-account transactions (trade in goods/services, operational income, business profits, dividends) may be settled through authorized dealers without discriminatory currency restrictions, subject to standard supporting documentation. However, WST is thinly traded and non-deliverable offshore: there is no unrestricted offshore interbank WST market, and all physical WST conversion occurs within Samoa or via limited correspondent lines. Capital-account transactions (shareholder equity injections above threshold, intercompany loans from non-residents, portfolio and direct investments, and repatriation of capital) require prior Central Bank approval or a 'no objection' confirmation from an authorized dealer under delegated authority. For a Samoa International Company (IC) operating exclusively offshore under the International Companies Act 1987, the Central Bank has granted exchange-control exemptions for external accounts: the WS_IC may hold, receive, and disburse USD and other foreign currencies without WST conversion restrictions, provided no transactions occur with Samoa residents, no business is conducted inside Samoa, and no liability is denominated in WST. Profit remittance and dividend repatriation from the IC are not subject to Samoan withholding tax or exchange-control encumbrances, but the underlying transfer must be documented as a legitimate current-account payment through an authorized dealer.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For onshore Samoan exporters, the Exchange Control Regulations 1976 require export proceeds to be remitted to an authorized dealer in Samoa within 31 days of shipment or the due date of payment, and the proceeds must generally be converted to WST unless the dealer holds a standing foreign-currency account approval for export retention. These surrender and mandatory conversion rules do NOT apply to the WS_IC because it is classified as an external/international company under the International Companies Act 1987: all export-style receipts from e-commerce platform settlements and cross-border trade may be retained in USD without WST conversion and without surrender deadlines. If any incidental WST credit arises on the IC account (e.g., refund from a local utility or erroneous inbound transfer), the funds must be converted to USD without delay and a written explanation provided to the authorized dealer.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD External Foreign Currency Account and Samoa International Company Operational Account
USD Corporate Operational Account with Pacific regional clearing capability
USD/WST Corporate Account with domestic correspondent dependency

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium viability as a primary on-island banking relationship. Airwallex, Wise, OFX, and similar offshore digital EMIs do not hold any Samoa banking or e-money license and cannot directly clear into the Samoa Interbank Network System (SINS) or maintain a settlement account with the Central Bank of Samoa. The WS_IC may use Airwallex as a supplementary cross-border payout rail for e-commerce disbursements, provided that (i) funds are staged in a tier-1 Samoan bank account, (ii) the EMI holds a valid licence and demonstrates a clean regulatory record in its home jurisdiction, (iii) the EMI onboarding accepts the Samoa IC's beneficial ownership documentation, and (iv) the Central Bank's authorized-dealer touchpoint rule is satisfied: every cross-border movement of funds must trace back to an authorized Samoan bank transfer. Crypto-backed or unlicensed digital EMIs, and any EMI that cannot produce a full audit trail of source of funds, are prohibited.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no Samoa statutory mandate requiring all directors or shareholders to appear physically in person to open an International Company account. In current practice, ANZ Bank (Samoa) and Bank of South Pacific (Samoa) require at least one authorized signatory or a director holding a valid power of attorney to attend an in-person or live video-conference KYC interview with the bank's compliance officer in Apia, supported by a Samoa-registered agent acting as introducer. Apostilled or legalized certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, memorandum and articles of association, register of directors and shareholders, and beneficial ownership declaration are mandatory. Remote onboarding is only available to existing bank clients with a strong relationship and a full bearing-witness introduction by the licensed agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity through nominee shareholders, bearer shares, or an offshore family trust holding the Samoa IC; banks face downgrade pressure from APG (Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering) and correspondent bank de-risking
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized beneficial ownership register extract or CBS-compliant statutory declaration identifying every ultimate beneficial owner (full legal name, date of birth, nationality, residential address); full trust deed, deed of amendment, and trustee resolution if the shareholder is a trust; registered-agent confirmation letter under the International Companies Act 1987; bank reference letters from the jurisdiction of incorporation of the parent; and a written economic substance narrative explaining the cross-border 3PL/fullfilment business, with client contracts, warehouse lease agreements, and inventory records demonstrating real commercial activity outside Samoa.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, small-ticket payment flows from e-commerce platforms (e.g., Amazon, Shopify, Temu, TikTok Shop) structured in a manner resembling an unlicensed money service business, remittance agent, or payment aggregator
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed marketplace or fulfilment-services agreements; payout statements from the platform showing order-level reference data; a value-chain description (buyer -> platform -> WS_IC -> logistics providers, freight forwarders, and last-mile carriers); management accounts and bank statements showing that inflows match fulfilment fees and outbound disbursements; and a written undertaking that the IC is not a 'money or value transfer service' under the Samoa AML/CFT Act 2007, but a warehouse operator and order-fulfilment agent classified under ISIC 5210/NAICS 493110.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party and split payments from Chinese, HK, US, or EU counterparties where invoice payee differs from the beneficial recipient, generating sanctions-evasion and fraudulent-transaction red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete supplier and counterparty registry with corporate KYC documents (certificate of incorporation, tax ID, director ID, licence); commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and customs entry for each disbursement; a third-party payment authorization letter ('letter of permission') signed by both the contracting party and the payee; internal sanctions-screening report run against OFAC, UN, EU, and Samoa Consolidated List; and transaction rationale memoranda maintained for 7 years for examiner review.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The parent or shareholder capital injection is routed via SWIFT MT103 from the originating tax-advantaged jurisdiction through a tier-1 Samoan authorized dealer. Samoa does not use standardized transaction purpose codes (e.g., Chinese-style SAFE codes); the wire narrative functions as the purpose declaration and must state clearly: 'INTERNATIONAL COMPANY EQUITY INJECTION – ISIC 5210 CROSS-DOCK FULFILMENT HUB WORKING CAPITAL'. The authorized dealer requires: certificate of incorporation and registration; board resolution authorizing the bank filing and the share allotment; share subscription/allotment documents; a source-of-funds statement (6-month bank statements or capital statement from the remitting entity); and confirmation that the injection is not derived from a restricted jurisdiction. If the capital originates from a PRC-related group entity, the remitting party must complete all SAFE outbound investment filings in China before submission to the Samoan bank. CBS prior approval is not required for an external IC account, but the bank must complete its 24-hour monitoring report as a 'high-value inward transfer'.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for high-value, time-critical trade settlements, using ANZ Bank (Samoa)'s Australian correspondent line or Bank of South Pacific (Samoa)'s regional Pacific/NZ lines with same-day or next-day value dating. For heavy procurement and cross-dock capital expenditure, the secondary rail is the Commercial Documentary Letter of Credit (UCP600), issued by ANZ/BSP Samoa in USD, payable at sight to suppliers and logistics vendors; standby LCs may be used to secure warehouse lease obligations. Local_ACH (SINS) is available only for Samoan-resident counterparties, which is generally irrelevant to this offshore 3PL structure. Bulk recurring payouts to multiple overseas subcontractors should be batched through bank-hosted host-to-host payment files or via an approved EMI (Airwallex) layered on top of the authorized-dealer account. The WS_IC should maintain multiple USD accounts at two tier-1 banks to ensure clearing redundancy and avoid single-counterparty liquidity risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards: Deliverable USD/WST forward contracts transacted with ANZ Bank (Samoa) or BSP Samoa only, supported by a documented underlying trade exposure; authorized-dealer approval is delegated for trade-backed forwards up to 12 months tenor; used exclusively to hedge any incidental Samoan-dollar operating costs or local regulatory payments.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): Offshore USD/WST NDFs booked through top-tier international banks (Australia/NZ based) referencing the Samoan Tala as a restricted-delivery currency; permitted for the WS_IC where the hedge is cash-settled offshore and no WST account conversion occurs; requires a written hedge rationale and matching of the USD exposure under the IC's treasury policy.

Cross-Currency Swaps and Plain Vanilla FX Swaps: USD/AUD, USD/NZD, or USD/EUR cross-currency swaps and rolling FX swaps are permissible for intercompany funding and temporary liquidity management through the authorized dealer, subject to CBS prior authorization for intercompany-loan hedging; WST-denominated cross-currency swaps are not viable in the absence of an offshore deliverable WST market and should be avoided.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form ICA-AR) with annual government fee payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of USD 100 per month or part thereof; continued default beyond 6 months exposes the company to administrative strike-off and restoration costs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrently with the Annual Return (within 30 days after incorporation anniversary)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to USD 2,000 per annum for non-filing or false filing; persistent failure may result in court-ordered strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Return (ESR) and Substance Notification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year (e.g., for calendar-year accounts, by 31 December of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default penalty of USD 1,000 per year; escalated to WST 10,000 for sustained non-compliance; possible strike-off and reporting to Competent Authority.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit required for an international company unless (i) the company's constitution mandates an audit; (ii) the company holds an activity license requiring audited accounts (e.g., banking, insurance, or digital services); or (iii) the Registrar issues a targeted audit direction for public-interest or non-compliance reasons. There are no revenue, asset, or member-count thresholds under the International Companies Act 1987.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or, with board resolution, another internationally accepted GAAP (e.g., US GAAP) may be used for the company's internal accounting records. Financial statements need not be filed with the Registrar or any Samoa tax authority.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the International Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2017, the company must identify all individuals who directly or indirectly own 25% or more of the share capital or voting rights, or who exercise ultimate effective control. An annual confirmation is filed with the Registrar at the same time as the annual return, restating each beneficial owner's full legal name, residential address, nationality, and the nature/quantum of control. Changes occurring during the year must be reported within 30 days of the change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 – 4,500 per audit engagement if voluntarily appointed

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% standard CIT for resident companies; International Company (IC) is statutorily exempt from Samoan CIT on all income other than Samoan-source income derived from a Samoan business
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: ICs under the International Companies Act 1987 enjoy full CIT exemption on foreign-source income; no capital gains tax; no stamp duty on share transfers; exemptions available for international shipping and certain financial services; annual government fee replaces CIT compliance

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IC Annual Return (Form IC-AR) and Annual Government Fee remittance payable to the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) through the SIFA e-Portal; no Samoan CIT return is filed for ICs deriving only foreign-source income
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing and annual fee payment due no later than 30 June annually, or within 30 days of the anniversary of incorporation, whichever is earlier per the International Companies Act and SIFA fee schedule

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name and registration number as recorded in the Samoa Companies Registry
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter exact name as per certificate of incorporation; non-resident beneficial owners are not required to be disclosed on this form

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered agent name, licence number, and Samoa physical address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The licensed Samoan registered agent must be identified; non-resident shareholders may not act as registered agent

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address in Samoa (may coincide with registered agent's office)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be a physical Samoan address; P.O. Box alone is insufficient

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors' names, nationalities, and tax residence status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors may be listed; Samoan tax residency of the director is determined by 183-day physical presence test

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Issued share capital and class of shares
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Minimum capital is not required; non-resident shareholders may hold 100% of issued shares

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual government fee computation based on authorised or issued share capital bracket
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fee schedule ranges from WST 200 to WST 5,000; compute per SIFA published tariff

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of no Samoan-source business activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the IC is engaged in cross-border e-commerce fulfillment only and holds no Samoan customers, affirm foreign-source income only to preserve CIT exemption

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge of WST 200 per month or part thereof; late payment of annual fee attracts 10% penalty on the unpaid fee; continued default triggers SIFA non-compliance notice, restoration fees, and strike-off with dissolution; directors may be personally fined up to WST 10,000 for knowingly supplying false information

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% under the Income Tax Act 2015 on dividends paid by a resident company to a non-resident; however, dividends paid by an exempt IC to non-resident shareholders are not subject to Samoan WHT because the IC is not liable to Samoan income tax and the dividend is treated as foreign-source income
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where a Samoan resident company is involved, claim DTA relief by submitting: (1) a Samoan Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the Ministry for Revenue; (2) a Beneficial Ownership Declaration; (3) the foreign treaty partner's TRC; (4) Form WHT-1 election to apply the reduced rate at source. For ICs, no WHT is levied on dividend distributions, so no treaty application is required unless the IC elects to be taxed as a Samoan resident or derives Samoan-source income. Samoa's DTAs with Australia and New Zealand provide 5% dividends for 10%+ holdings and 15% otherwise; no Samoan WHT applies to DTA-protected IC distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: interest 15%, royalties 15% if paid by a Samoan resident. ICs paying foreign royalties or interest to non-residents are not subject to Samoan WHT because such payments are treated as foreign-source. Treaty rates under the Australia and New Zealand DTAs: interest 10%, royalties 10%. No Samoan domestic WHT applies to cross-border e-commerce IP royalties paid through an IC structure, provided no Samoan permanent establishment exists.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory Local File or Master File threshold is prescribed under Samoan law; Transfer Pricing Rules under the Income Tax Act 2015 apply the OECD arm's length principle to all cross-border related-party transactions, including management fees, software licensing, and logistics sub-contracting. Prudent practice requires contemporaneous documentation when annual related-party turnover exceeds WST 1,000,000 equivalent.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa does not impose Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, the International Companies Act 1987 requires each IC to maintain a licensed registered agent and a physical registered office in Samoa, and to keep adequate accounting records reflecting economic activities. The OECD Global Forum reviews Samoa's transparency standards; ICs must demonstrate substantive business presence in Samoa to avoid being characterised as a shell company and to preserve the CIT exemption.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (False Declaration of Foreign-Source Income)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a declaration of no Samoan-source activity while conduct or receipt of revenue from Samoan customers exceeds 60 days of physical presence or constitutes a Samoan permanent establishment (e.g., local warehousing for Samoan buyers)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the tax evaded; late payment interest at 2% per month; fine up to WST 100,000; imprisonment up to 7 years under the Tax Administration Act 2015; forfeiture of IC exempt status and retroactive CIT assessment at 27%
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false declarations are jointly and severally liable for the ICA, WHT, and interest; civil restitution orders; travel bans; disqualification as director for 10 years; criminal imprisonment up to 7 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a passive nominee without Samoan registered agent, registered office, accounting records, or a demonstrable business purpose; failing to file annual returns for two consecutive years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SIFA strike-off and dissolution; restoration fee up to WST 1,000; reinstatement by court order; automatic loss of limited liability for all debts incurred after strike-off; Samoan Ministry for Revenue may disregard corporate personality and assess the beneficial owner personally
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers personally liable for company debts if the IC is struck off with no solvent winding up; statutory restitution of misappropriated assets; prohibition against holding a Samoan registered agent licence

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering / Counter-Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The IC or its registered agent accepts cash proceeds known to be derived from fraud, customs evasion, or sanctions circumvention in the e-commerce fulfillment chain, without filing a suspicious transaction report to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to WST 2,000,000 for the corporate entity under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter- Financing of Terrorism Act 2018; asset freezing; cancellation of the registered agent's licence; criminal penalty of imprisonment up to 10 years for money laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for fines up to WST 500,000; criminal imprisonment up to 10 years; confiscation of personal assets; exclusion from banking services in Samoa and partner jurisdictions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Failure (Resident IC with Samoan-Source Income)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An IC that inadvertently becomes Samoan-resident (by conducting a Samoan trade or business) fails to withhold 15% WHT on dividends, interest, or royalties paid to non-residents
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding tax recovery from the IC; penalty of 50% of the unpaid WHT; interest on unpaid amounts at 2% monthly; refusal of deduction for the underlying expense; customs and border enforcement of tax debts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the unremitted WHT if they knowingly directed the payment without withholding; criminal fine up to WST 50,000; disqualification from serving on any Samoa-registered company board

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation (Related-Party Cross-Border E-commerce Fees)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting an excessive management fee or IP royalty charge from a related Hong Kong or Singapore entity that erodes Samoan taxable base without satisfying the arm's length principle; absence of contemporaneous benchmarking documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of assessable income by Samoa Revenue; secondary adjustment deemed distribution; penalty of 40% of the transfer pricing adjustment; interest accrual; publication of the taxpayer's name on a non-compliance register
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved inflated related-party payments may be assessed for reckless tax conduct; civil penalty of 20% of the adjusted amount; travel restriction pending full payment; personal liability extends to foreign directors with no Samoan physical presence
